passages.original: ab illa perditionis massa quæ facta est per primum Adam, debemus intelligere ncminrm posse discerni, nisi qui hoc donum habet, quisquis hahet, qnod gratia Salvatoris accepit3. Hoc amem apostolicum testimonium tam magnum est, ut beatus Cyprianus ad Quirinum scribens, ipsum subjecerit illi titulo, in quo ait, In nullo esse gloriandum, quiudo nostrum nibil sit (Lib. 3 Testimoniorum, titulo seu cap. 4).
passages.english: we ought to understand that no one can be set apart from that mass of perdition which came about through the first Adam except one who has this gift; and whoever has it has received it by the grace of the Saviour. This apostolic testimony is so great that the blessed Cyprian, writing to Quirinus, placed it under that heading in which he says: "That we must glory in nothing, since nothing is our own" (Book 3 of the Testimonies, heading or chapter 4).
passages.notes: The passage begins mid-sentence, continuing "when we hear, 'For who sets you apart?...'" (1 Cor. 4:7) from the preceding context. Scanning errors corrected: ncminrm = neminem, hahet = habet, qnod = quod, amem = autem, quiudo = quando, nibil = nihil; the stray "3" after accepit is a footnote mark.
